title: Standard smooth algebras lift across any quotient of the base ring
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $I\subset R$ an ideal, and $C$ a standard smooth commutative $R/I$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-algebra]. There exist a standard smooth commutative $R$-algebra $B$ and an $R/I$-algebra isomorphism $B/IB\cong C$, where $IB$ is the ideal generated by the image of $I$ in $B$. No nilpotence hypothesis is imposed on $I$.

proof.text: Choose a finite submersive presentation of the standard smooth R/I-algebra C. Lift all coefficients of its equations fbar to equations f over R, preserving the finite index sets and the injection selecting the Jacobian minor variables. Form B = R[x,z]/(f,z D - 1), where D is the selected Jacobian determinant of f. The enlarged Jacobian matrix is block triangular with diagonal blocks the selected matrix and D, so its determinant is D squared. This is a unit in B because z D = 1. Thus B is standard smooth over R.

Reduction of coefficients modulo I commutes with partial derivatives and determinants. Therefore B/IB is (R/I)[x,z]/(fbar,z Dbar - 1). The presentation map sends x to the generators of C and z to the inverse of the image of Dbar; it kills each relation. Conversely the classes of x give a map from C to B/IB. The composites fix the x generators; they also fix z, since z and the image of Dbar inverse are both inverses of Dbar. Hence the maps are inverse R/I-algebra maps. Transport B along ULift to the carrier universe max(u,v). This argument works for zero rings and empty lists as well.
